h1: Make more of your Denver back yard.
lede: Plan pet turf, a lawn or a putting green around the garage, patio and trees you want to keep. Start with a free visit and written estimate.
wins: Use the space between house and garage
Plan pet areas with cleaning in mind
Keep trees and access in the layout

answer.question: Can turf fit a small Denver yard with an alley garage?
answer.answer: Yes, a layout can work around the garage, gate and patio while reserving a lawn, pet area or putting green. The free visit helps compare those choices. Show us the narrowest access and any tree roots or wet spots that could affect preparation.

blocks.h2: Use the narrow shape to your advantage.
paras: A longer putting line may fit where a wide green will not. Decide which putts matter to you and leave walking room beside the surface. Keep the route to the garage useful after the work is finished.

Older city yards can have changed levels and buried remnants from past work. Show us known issues and ask for preparation and unresolved conditions to be stated in the estimate. Check City and any association requirements for the actual proposal. Berkley itself is unincorporated Adams County, not the City and County of Denver (Wikipedia).

blocks.h2: Where the grass gave up, turf stays green.
paras: If the dog wears the route between the door and alley gate, start there. A defined pet area can leave room for seating and planting instead of covering the entire yard, with waste pickup and cleaning access built into the layout.

By August, plenty of Denver back yards look alike: a detached garage off the alley, an elm or honeylocust shading most of what's left, and a dog wearing a track through the rest. Bluegrass wants sun and a rest from traffic, and a small shaded yard gives it neither, so it thins to dirt and turns to mud after rain.

Artificial turf doesn't need sun, so the tree can stay and the lawn still looks like one. Pet turf drains where the dog goes and rinses clean with a hose, which ends the muddy paws at the back door. On a free visit we measure the space and check the ground, then draw a custom layout around the garage, the trunk and the gate, and you approve it before any work starts.

blocks.h2: Old Denver sits on fill, so the ground check comes first.
paras: Around Washington Park and Congress Park, the USDA soil survey maps the ground as urban land and two soils, Elyria and Racas, both classed as spolic: material moved there by people. Beneath that fill lies smectitic clay, the kind that swells when it gets wet (USDA Soil Data Access).

Fill is uneven. Its depth can change from one side of a yard to the other, it can hide old brick, ash and rubble, and the survey rates the Elyria soil somewhat poorly drained. The lots are close to flat, so the work here is in the base, not the grade.

So we open the ground before we build on it: site prep and a base made for what's actually there, which keeps the surface level over swelling clay and sends rain down and away rather than across the top.

blocks.h2: Two watering days, drought pricing and no turf rebate.
paras: Denver Water declared a Stage 1 drought on 25 March 2026 (Denver Water). Single-family homes water on two assigned days a week, even addresses on Sunday and Thursday and odd addresses on Wednesday and Saturday, and never between 10 a.m. and 6 p.m. Apartments, businesses and HOAs get Tuesday and Friday only.

For 2026 the board has also ended the lawn-watering season, with no lawn watering or spray irrigation after 30 September (Denver Water). Temporary drought pricing adds a charge to higher water use through 30 April 2027 (Denver Water).

Don't count on a rebate to pay for turf. Denver Water's lawn-removal discount, up to $750 through Resource Central for taking out at least 200 square feet, needs a planted water-wise design, and artificial turf is not allowed (Denver Water). What turf buys you is a yard that's off the schedule for good; the water rebates guide covers the rest of the metro.

Berkley isn't billed by Denver directly, but the same rules reach it. Most of the neighborhood, roughly 52nd Avenue to 60th and Sheridan Boulevard to Tejon Street, sits in the Berkeley Water and Sanitation District, which has bought all its water from Denver Water since 1 January 2018 (Berkeley Water and Sanitation District). The eastern edge, Tennyson Street to I-25 and 56th Avenue to Sherrylwood Lane, falls in Crestview Water and Sanitation District, which posts drought notices under a shared Denver Water Restrictions Resolution (Crestview Water and Sanitation District). Either way, the Stage 1 watering days, the 30 September cutoff and the missing turf rebate above apply the same in Berkley as they do in Denver.

blocks.h2: Crestmoor, Belcaro Park and the landmark districts still ask first.
paras: In Crestmoor Park (2nd Filing), the homeowners association's design guidelines count landscaping, a change of grade, ground level or drainage pattern as "Development" that needs Architectural Review Committee approval before it starts, most recently revised 19 May 2026 (Crestmoor Park (2nd Filing) Homes Association Design Guidelines). Inside the 8-foot side setbacks the guidelines allow only landscaping, so turf can run to the line but a wall, structure or edging there cannot. The guidelines do set a turf rule: premium artificial turf is accepted only with a full specification and sample submitted for ARC approval, only plush rolled goods with a natural look are considered, and interlocking turf squares are forbidden outright, so send the ARC your layout and product details before work starts (Crestmoor Park Homes Association).

Belcaro Park is an architectural HOA with covenants, split into four filings that each carry their own covenant document (Belcaro Park Homeowners Association, maps and covenants by filing). No turf rule is published on its public pages, so a project there needs the covenant for that filing and the association's procedures packet for architectural projects before you plan a layout.

Country Club and Denver's other landmark historic districts follow the city's landmark design guidelines for site and landscape design, dated 27 January 2016 in the document's own footer. Guideline 5.4a asks owners to keep most of a historic front yard as a grass lawn or a designed xeriscape that still reads as a landscaped yard, and guideline 5.4d says not to add berms that weren't historically there; the same rule reaches a street-facing side yard on a corner lot (Denver Landmark Guidelines: Site & Landscape Design). Turf itself isn't mentioned, so ask Landmark Preservation staff whether a front-yard install needs review before you plan one. A back yard in one of these districts that also sits in an HOA still falls under the state line that makes a covenant against nonvegetative turf there unenforceable (C.R.S. 37-60-126).

faq.q: Who installs artificial turf in Denver, CO?
faq.a: We install artificial turf, pet turf and backyard putting greens in Denver, CO. Two things set Denver yards apart: old shade trees that starve a lawn of sun, and ground the USDA maps as fill over swelling clay. Denver Water's rebates leave artificial turf out, so the payoff is a yard that stays green without a watering day. Call 303-349-2368 for a free estimate.

faq.q: Is artificial turf a good fit for a dog in a small Denver yard?
faq.a: Yes. Pet turf drains where the dog goes and hoses clean, and a dog can't turn it to mud the way it does a shaded lawn. Put the dog's area where the afternoon shade falls, because shade does more than anything else to keep turf cool.

faq.q: Does Denver Water pay anything toward turf for an HOA or a business?
faq.a: No. Its Landscape Transformation Assistance Program won't fund HOA or commercial designs that include artificial turf, landscape fabric or hardscape (Denver Water). The state's limit on non-functional turf also covers a business's new landscaping and an HOA's new common areas, though turf for fields of play is exempt (SB24-005).

faq.q: Can I fit a putting green in a Denver back yard?
faq.a: A green with real break and a few cups can fit between a garage and a patio. Denver's public courses, from City Park and Wellshire to Kennedy's 18 holes and the Harvard Gulch par 3, are there for the long game. Under state law a putting green counts as functional turf (HB25-1113).

faq.q: Do I need anyone's permission for turf in my Denver back yard?
faq.a: Not always, but don't assume an older neighborhood has no HOA to ask: Crestmoor, Belcaro Park and Denver's landmark historic districts add a review step, the same as Central Park or Lowry. Where a covenant HOA exists, a covenant that bans nonvegetative turf in a back yard is unenforceable (C.R.S. 37-60-126). Front-yard work and design details are still the HOA's call, or Landmark Preservation's in a historic district.

faq.q: Is Berkley part of Denver, and do these rules apply there?
faq.a: Berkley is an unincorporated community in Adams County, not the City and County of Denver (Wikipedia). Water is a different story: the Berkeley Water and Sanitation District has bought all its water from Denver Water since 2018 (Berkeley Water and Sanitation District), and Crestview Water and Sanitation District on the eastern edge posts the same Denver Water drought notice (Crestview Water and Sanitation District). The watering days, the cutoff date and the missing turf rebate above apply either way.
